lines.text: You freelance for three clients. One agent works across all of them, and the details start to blur together.
Then one morning the agent asks which repo it is in, and nobody is quite sure. That is how a bank key lands in a retail site.
Clients notice mistakes like that. You end up checking every task by hand, and the agent saves you no time at all.
Agent R Q fixes this with workspaces. Each client gets a workspace of its own, a clean room for their work.
Every workspace has its own tasks, its own history, and its own live event stream. Nothing is shared by accident.
Each one also has its own M C P token. The agent for client B simply cannot see client A.
Open client A in the morning, and only client A tasks are there. Nothing to filter and nothing to remember.
Use a different agent per client if you like. Claude on the retail site, Codex on the bank app, Gemini on the blog.
When one agent needs you, only that workspace lights up, so a question from client B never gets buried.
If a client leaves, you rotate or delete that one token, and the other two workspaces keep working untouched.
When the project is finished, the whole story of that client is in one place, ready to hand over or look back on.
One client, one lane. Try workspaces for your own client work at Agent R Q dot com.
